find_locations.description: Turn a place name into the exact values The Muse's location filter accepts - 'seattle' becomes 'Seattle, WA'. Worth doing before filtering on a location read from a spreadsheet, an email or an earlier step: The Muse answers a place it does not recognise by quietly returning the remote-only listings rather than an error, so an unchecked value comes back looking like a successful search with the wrong jobs in it. list_jobs_published_since.description: The roles published on or after a date - what a daily or weekly job alert is built on. The Muse's API has no date filter and no newest-first ordering, so this reads the filtered listing page by page and keeps the postings dated on or after the day given. It reports how far it read, so 'nothing new' and 'nothing new in the pages read' are told apart.

search_jobs.description: Find jobs whose wording contains every word given - 'staff python' or 'nurse practitioner'. The Muse's API has no keyword search of its own, so this reads the filtered listing page by page and matches as it goes: set the filters as narrowly as you can, and raise 'Most pages to read' when you want it to look further. It reports how far it read and whether it reached the end, so 'nothing found' and 'nothing in the first hundred' are told apart.
